Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-21
Time: 16:00 UTC (55m)
Attendees: Jared Morales, Priya Nair, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Tom Ellis, Maya Chen, Derek O'Neal, Sofia Ramirez (Windward)

Summary (auto):
Kickoff for Windward Labs activation: align on network requirements, Dedicated vs Hosted gating, pilot success metrics, and security artifacts. Plan: small Dedicated sandbox, network peering, quick quantization/cost tune, and a bench of acceptance tests.

Topics:
- VPC & peering
- Data residency & KMS/HSM
- Sizing Dedicated pool for bursty inference (chat + embeddings)
- Rollout plan and success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, SLOs)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Jared from Redwood, AE, joined by Priya, our solutions eng, and Liam from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom: Good, thanks. Morning for us. We wanted to get this kickoff aligned, we've got a few exec stakes here and want to make sure the network bits don't block us.
[00:16] Priya: Great. Big picture — we hear you want predictable latency for the chat front-end and low-cost batch embeddings for search. We'll propose a small Dedicated pool for the pilot with burst capacity to hosted.
[00:26] Maya: Quick note — our infra team is strict on VPC peering, no public egress for inference. So we'll need the private deployment flow or VPC-hosted Dedicated.
[00:36] Liam: Totally, that lines up with our Redwood Private options — you can run the control plane in our cloud while traffic stays in your VPC, or run a full private package if needed.
[00:45] Derek: Also want to flag model choices; we currently evalf - sorry, evalled a couple of open models, and we care about token cost; we might want quantized variants. How's Redwood handling int8/4 quant?
[00:57] Priya: Good question. We support quantized model profiles; our runtime picks kernels and can run 8-bit or 4-bit in many configs. For chat we prefer 8-bit to keep latency predictable; we can bench both.
[01:12] Speaker 1: (background) I had a quick question about logs...
[01:18] Sofia: Yes, on logs — we need audit logs, per-request lineage, and to limit PII retention. Does Redwood provide token-level tracing?
[01:29] Priya: We have per-request traces in the Console, and you can disable retention or redact inputs. For compliance, we integrate KMS for envelope encryption and we have SOC2 docs we can share.
[01:41] Tom: Awesome, please share SOC2. Also curious about latency SLOs; we expect p95 under 250ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). Is that realistic?
[01:53] Jared: For that SLA, Dedicated is the right route. Our Dedicated pools are sized to meet p95 targets; we'll run an initial benchmark with your sample traffic. If absolutely necessary, we can do auto fallback to hosted models if capacity hits constraints.
[02:06] Maya: Network — we'll need a sample Terraform snippet for peering and a list of IPs and ports.
[02:12] Jared: We'll share the VPC checklist and Terraform example. I'll put that in the follow-up with links.
[02:18] Priya: For the pilot sizing, can you give us traffic patterns? QPS peaks, average session lengths?
[02:25] Derek: Typical chat peak around 60 QPS, but bursts to 150 QPS for marketing events. Embedding pipeline is batched overnight, about 100k docs per day.
[02:34] Priya: Ok that helps. For chat at 150 QPS bursts we'll suggest a small Dedicated cluster with autoscale policy and a warm standby. For embeddings, we'll propose a batch node pool tuned for throughput, with batching windows.
[02:46] Tom: Are there per-hour cost surprises with warm standby? We're a bit cost sensitive.
[02:52] Jared: There is overhead for reserved capacity; we'll surface a cost model. Our Optimize tooling will give recommended batching, caching and quant settings to hit your cost target.
[03:02] Maya: What's caching look like? We have repeated prefixes for some flows.
[03:06] Priya: Prefix/KV caching is supported; it cuts token cost significantly for repeated content. We can suggest TTLs and cache keys for your flows.
[03:14] Liam: Quick ops note — we can provision a sandbox Dedicated cluster within 3–5 business days once we have CIDR ranges.
[03:22] Derek: Good. On acceptance tests, we'd like a simple suite: 95th latency, cost per 1k tokens, and correctness baseline on a prompt set.
[03:32] Priya: We'll share a test harness (lightweight) you can run; it returns latency distributions and token accounting.
[03:38] Speaker 1: (mumbles) where do we store keys...
[03:41] Sofia: KMS — we require customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed. Is that supported?
[03:48] Priya: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; our Private deployments can integrate HSMs or your cloud KMS. We'll attach an architecture note.
[03:54] Tom: Any regulatory issues with data residency? Some of our customers are EU-only. Can we pin regions?
[04:01] Jared: You can pin model serving region to EU. For Private on-prem, data never leaves your network. We'll document the region controls.
[04:10] Maya: On auth — SSO + RBAC. We need SAML with SCIM provisioning.
[04:16] Priya: Supported. We have SAML + SCIM templates and role-based policies; will include a sample mapping.
[04:23] Derek: Curious about model fallback behavior — if our Dedicated is saturated, what happens?
[04:29] Jared: We have smart routing. Policy options: queue, fail-fast, or fallback to hosted variant. Most customers use a fallback to a cost-compatible hosted model as graceful degradation. We'll align on your preference.
[04:42] Tom: We prefer fallback over errors for customer-facing chat.
[04:45] Priya: Noted. We'll set fallback policy in the rollout plan.
[04:50] Maya: Do we get trace IDs per request so we can link latency spikes to code?
[04:55] Liam: Yes, trace IDs emitted and you can forward traces to your tracing system via a webhook or OTLP.
[05:02] Sofia: About data deletion — are there guarantees for ephemeral storage?
[05:07] Priya: We support configurable retention policies and immediate purge on request; we'll add that to the security sheet.
[05:13] Derek: Can we schedule a bench with a sample model and our prompt set, like next week?
[05:18] Jared: Yes, Priya can run the bench and invite you to the results session. Priya, are you available next Tuesday?
[05:23] Priya: I am. Tuesday 14:00 UTC works for me.
[05:26] Maya: Works for us.
[05:28] Jared: Great — we'll book that.
[05:31] Priya: For the bench I'll want: a representative prompt set (you mentioned marketing bursts), example session flows, CIDR ranges for DBS peering, and an example embedding pipeline sample.
[05:43] Tom: We'll provide those. Also want the Dedicated sizing worksheet to review for budget.
[05:48] Jared: I'll send the pricing + Dedicated sizing.
[05:51] Liam: Quick recap, I'll put together the runbook link: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/windward-labs (placeholder) and the VPC checklist.
[05:58] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:01] Sofia: Last item — we want an internal stakeholder list for approvals; I'll send names to Jared.
[06:06] Jared: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the bench.
